title: Control-plane security fix: close the readonly_agent_guard PowerShell/scripting write gap (G5 M0-T102 MEDIUM advisory)
objective: Close the confirmed enforcement gap in .claude/hooks/readonly_agent_guard.py (G5 M0-T102 finding): (i) extend the PreToolUse matcher in .claude/settings.json to cover every write-capable shell tool the harness exposes on Windows (PowerShell, not only Bash); (ii) add a PowerShell mutation/redirection denylist mirroring the Bash pass (Set-Content, Out-File, Add-Content, New-Item, Move-Item, Remove-Item, Tee-Object, [IO.File]::Write*, redirection operators, git via PowerShell) with the same fail-closed-on-unparseable envelope; (iii) treat the scripting-language class generally (python -c file writes share the failure mode - document the residual honestly if not fully closable); (iv) regression tests analogous to the existing Bash tests, RED-on-mutant. Also reduce read-only false positives observed by M0-T102 reviewers (python -c pure reads containing open( were transiently denied). Land BEFORE any unit C-I reviewer dispatch into a write-capable working tree (G5 recommendation).
business_reason: G5 M0-T102: a reviewer agent could mutate the working tree through PowerShell despite the read-only guard; machine enforcement must replace the procedural stopgap.
outputs: .claude/hooks/readonly_agent_guard.py (PowerShell/scripting write interception, fail-closed envelope, reduced read-only false positives)
regression tests for the guard (RED-on-mutant) alongside the existing guard tests
